topIssues.title: op: remove the cross-unsafe chain-head notion from Go (op-node, op-service, op-devstack)
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Go-side mirror of #22519's kona change: the cross-unsafe **chain-head** notion is op-supervisor-era vestige — nothing in the current interop design (op-supernode) produces a distinct cross-unsafe head; it just shadows unsafe. Remove it so there is only "unsafe" (permalinks at `3233dd8b`):

- **op-node** cross-unsafe head plumbing: [`PromoteCrossUnsafeEvent`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/3233dd8bde590372e5820ae9f68c5b2c25e8ba51/op-node/rollup/engine/events.go#L48-L53), [`EngineController.SetCrossUnsafeHead`/`crossUnsafeHead`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/3233dd8bde590372e5820ae9f68c5b2c25e8ba51/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L507-L527), the [`OnCrossUnsafeUpdate` status-tracker path](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/3233dd8bde590372e5820ae9f68c5b2c25e8ba51/op-node/rollup/status/status.go#L147-L152).
- **op-service**: the [`eth.SyncStatus.CrossUnsafeL2`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/3233dd8bde590372e5820ae9f68c5b2c25e8ba51/op-service/eth/sync_status.go#L36-L38) field (removed from the wire — `optimism_syncStatus` and everything embedding the struct; kona already dropped its counterpart in #22519), and [`supervisor_status.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/3233dd8bde590372e5820ae9f68c5b2c25e8ba51/op-service/eth/supervisor_status.go) if dead.
- **op-devstack / tests**: the `safety.CrossUnsafe` chain-head mappings in `dsl/l2_cl.go` / `dsl/l2_el.go`, the `l2_network.go` debug dump, and the tests reading `CrossUnsafeL2` (two acceptance tests + one op-node test).

**Boundary — keep the message-safety level.** `safety.Level`'s `cross-unsafe` value stays: it is the live `minSafety` parameter of op-interop-filter's access-list check API ([backend.go#L373-L374](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/3233dd8bde590372e5820ae9f68c5b2c25e8ba51/op-interop-filter/filter/backend.go#L373-L374) supports exactly `local-unsafe` and `cross-unsafe`), sent by op-reth's tx-pool filter client and configured in op-interop-mon. That is a per-message validation threshold, not a chain-head label — removing it would delete functionality (the stricter admission mode) and break a wire contract, so it is out of scope here.

**Caveats:** dropping `CrossUnsafeL2` changes op-node's production `optimism_syncStatus` response (Go JSON clients tolerate absent fields, but out-of-repo readers should get a release note); check the specs/docs for a cross-unsafe safety-level definition. Independent of the kona PRs — only a trivial textual overlap in `rust/kona/tests/node/restart/sequencer_restart_test.go`.

Part of #22547.

topIssues.title: kona-sp1-proposer: Don't build games off of invalid anchor states
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body: When the anchor state is invalid (e.g. set to zero during a new devnet) the proposer might try to build a game off of it, which it then cannot prove. It should have stronger sanity checks around the anchor state and not build on top of invalid anchor states (and warn loudly if it detects this case).

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: build shared scenario world
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

* Add a crate-private `ScenarioWorld` shared by fake L1, superroot, clock, proof, and action ports.
* Model immutable L1 snapshots, independent clocks and visibility, scripted failures, transaction lifecycles, barriers, and target-aware journals.
* Use the real prestate cache with zero retry delay and support prestate publication, initialization, and proposer restart.
* Add deterministic scenario coverage for confirmations, concurrent tasks, signer serialization, transaction uncertainty, failure boundaries, and restart behavior.

## Why

The existing fakes work well for focused tests, but they make longer proposer histories difficult to set up and reason about. This adds a shared world so effects from one cycle, such as a confirmed transaction, are visible to later reads, while tests retain precise control over timing, failures, and blocked tasks. This provides the foundation for the upcoming policy scenarios without adding production test hooks.

Part of #22171

topPRs.title: kona!: add chain_id metric label
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Part of #22529.

**Before.** kona's metrics carry no chain dimension. In a single-chain kona-node that is fine, but in a multi-chain lokahi process every chain's series collapse into one — `kona_node_block_labels{label="unsafe"}` would flap between chains instead of showing each one.

**After.** Every metric emitted by kona's `engine`, `gossip`, `disc`, `rpc`, `derive`, `providers-local`, `providers-alloy` and `node-service` crates carries a `chain_id` label. No metric is renamed; one metric's label set changes, see below.

**How.** Each metric owner already has its chain ID (or its `RollupConfig`) in scope, so the label is threaded from what is already there rather than plumbed in: `EngineState` gains a `chain_id` field, long-lived components cache an `Arc<str>` label instead of formatting per emit, and `Metrics::init`/`zero` take the chain ID so the pre-created series are labelled too. The label key and its `Arc<str>` constructor live in `kona-macros`, so the seven `Metrics` types share one spelling rather than seven. `set!` and `record!` gained variadic-label arms — only `inc!` had one, so no `set!`/`record!` site could express two labels.

**Drift found on the way.** Labelling `zero()` meant walking every pre-created series against its emit sites, and a number of them disagreed: `dial_peer_error`, `find_node_requests`, `gossip_events`, `rpc_calls`, `chain_rpc_calls`, the engine task list (the `seal` task was missing), the `block_validation_failed` reasons (`parent_beacon_root` is produced by no error arm), and the beacon-client, L2-provider and buffered-provider method strings now all match what is emitted. `banned_peers` is no longer pre-created, since its `peer_id` has no finite value set. `kona_node_gossipsub_events`, `kona_providers_local_cache_capacity` and `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes` were pre-created but never emitted by anything, and are removed rather than multiplied by the number of chains. Three components also still emitted process-wide: the node builds one `OnlineBeaconClient` and one `OnlineBlobProvider` per chain, and `BlobSource`/`CalldataSource` already receive the `RollupConfig`, so all four take the chain ID now.

BREAKING CHANGE: `kona_node_engine_task_failure` changes shape. It previously used the task name as the label *key* with the severity as its value (`{insert="critical"}`), so every task type minted a new label key and the series `Metrics::zero()` pre-created was never the one incremented. It now emits `{type="insert",severity="critical",chain_id="..."}`, matching `kona_node_engine_task_count`. Operators with panels or alert rules selecting `kona_node_engine_task_failure{insert=...}` (or `consolidate`/`build`/`finalize`) must migrate them to `{type="insert",severity="critical"}`. No in-repo Grafana dashboard selects this metric, so the blast radius is external dashboards only.

BREAKING CHANGE: the Rust API of the affected crates changes too, for downstream consumers who depend on them directly.

- Three public constants are removed: `Metrics::GOSSIPSUB_EVENT` (`kona-gossip`), `Metrics::CACHE_CAPACITY` (`kona-providers-local`) and `Metrics::CACHE_MEMORY_USAGE` (`kona-providers-alloy`). No time series disappears with them — nothing in the workspace ever emitted any of the three.
- `Metrics::init()` and `Metrics::zero()` now take a `chain_id: u64` on all seven `Metrics` types, and about twenty component constructors gain the same parameter, several of them losing `const` to build the label. The ones most likely to be constructed downstream are `BlobSource::new`, `CalldataSource::new`, `AlloyChainProvider::new`/`new_http`/`new_with_trust`, `ConnectionGater::new` and the `kona-derive` stage constructors. (`AlloyL2ChainProvider` is unaffected — it already took the `RollupConfig`.)
- `EngineSyncState::apply_update` is now module-private; use `EngineState::apply_sync_update(update)`, which supplies the chain ID from the state it already holds.
- `OnlineBlobProvider` and `OnlineBeaconClient` are the exception: they gain a `with_chain_id(chain_id)` builder method and a public field, so existing construction keeps compiling unchanged.

---

topPRs.title: kona-engine: local/cross-safe vocabulary and a single cross-safe promotion entry point
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Part of #22525. Stacked on #22519.

**Before.** One head called `safe_head`, written from four places: payload insert, both consolidation paths, and the reset start-point. Under interop that head has to mean two things at once — locally derived, and cross-chain verified — and nothing in the types said which.

**After.** Two heads. `local_safe_head` is what derivation advances; `cross_safe_head` is the forkchoice `safeBlockHash`. `EngineSyncStateUpdate` has no cross-safe field, so the four old writers cannot express a cross-safe move at all — they are local-safe-only. Wire names are unchanged: `safe_l2`, the `safe` metric label, `subscribe_safe_head`.

**How.** Moving the cross-safe head requires a `CrossSafePromotion`, which has no public constructor. Outside `kona-engine` one can only be minted by the engine's `CrossSafePromoter`, handed out once by `Engine::with_external_cross_safe`. Standalone kona-node uses `Engine::new`, where `CrossSafeSource::LocalSafe` mints the trivial promotion inline, so a local-safe advance still reports local-safe == cross-safe in a single forkchoice call. Promotions may move backwards — that is how an interop rewind unwinds a decision — but are clamped at the finalized head. The depth-1 lockstep confirmation to the derivation actor now carries local-safe; driving it from cross-safe would deadlock under interop, since the promotion it would wait on itself waits on every chain's derivation.

**Review fixes.** Three behavioural changes landed after review, each with a regression test. A finality signal for a block that is not yet cross-safe is now dropped with a `warn!` rather than failing `Critical` and killing the engine actor — a routine interop state, so the producer-side fix is tracked separately in #22582. Cross-safe promotion is clamped at `local_safe_head` above as well as `finalized_head` below, warning on each, so it can no longer send `safeBlockHash` past `headBlockHash`. And initial-forkchoice emission is tracked by an explicit `forkchoice_emitted` flag instead of comparing the sync state against `Default`, which never fired for an externally promoted engine.

New tests hold cross-safe behind local-safe by withholding promotion and assert the resulting FCU labels and sync-status fields, plus the backward-promotion clamp and the standalone single-FCU path.

## Summary

- add a Kona-SP1 proposer DSL backed by the shared devstack Prometheus client, with exact same-snapshot expectations and explicit metrics-disabled diagnostics
- replace acceptance-facing proposer metrics endpoints with cached runtime handles and distinct automatic/delayed lifecycle behavior
- add ZK game helpers for immediate/temporal unproven verification and composable proven-by waits, then cut the ZK acceptance scenarios over to the DSL

## Test plan

- [x] mise exec -- just build-superchain-go
- [x] mise exec -- go test ./op-devstack/devtest/metrics ./op-devstack/dsl/zkproposer ./op-devstack/dsl/proofs ./op-devstack/sysgo ./op-devstack/presets
- [x] mise exec -- go test -run ^$ ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs/zk
- [x] focused invalid-game and concurrent-defense ZK acceptance scenarios (547.028s)
- [x] full ZK acceptance package on the final reviewed source (851.486s)
- [x] mise exec -- just lint-go

## Notes

The common op-devstack metrics implementation and the existing op-dispute-mon DSL are unchanged. Interop-monitor registry assertions and load-test graph collection remain intentionally in-process/test-owned.

topPRs.title: feat(kona-safedb): port op-node SafeDB to Rust
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds the **`kona-safedb`** crate — a 1-to-1 Rust port of the op-node `safedb` package. It records, per L1 block, the L2 safe head that derivation reached as of that block, used by systems (fault proofs, interop) that need a high-quality derivation record. kona-node previously had no equivalent.

The on-disk key/value encoding is byte-exact with the Go implementation, so a database is interchangeable between the two.

## What's included

- **`SafeDbV1` trait** — the versioned database interface, mockable via `#[cfg_attr(test, mockall::automock)]` (generates `MockSafeDbV1`).
- **`SafeDb`** — rocksdb-backed implementation. All Go methods ported: `safe_head_updated`, `safe_head_reset`, `safe_head_at_l1`, `first_entry`, `last_entry`, `l1_at_safe_head`, `enabled`, `close`.
- **`DisabledDb`** — no-op implementation (port of `disabled.go`).
- The rocksdb backend is behind a **non-default `rocksdb` feature**, so consumers needing only the trait/`DisabledDb` avoid the rocksdb/libclang build dependency. Default `cargo build --workspace` does not pull rocksdb; `--all-features` (used by CI test/clippy) builds and exercises everything.
- Iterators are bounded to the key column, mirroring the Go `IterRange`.

## Testing

- Full Go test suite ported (store/reopen persistence, reset truncation edge cases, `l1_at_safe_head` table, decode/ordering).
- Added exact-byte-layout tests (locking cross-impl interop) and a backend-error test.
- `--all-features`: 30 tests pass. Default: build is warning-free. `clippy --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo doc -D warnings`, `cargo +nightly fmt --check`, and `cargo hack check --feature-powerset` all clean.

## Out of scope (follow-up)

Node integration — `SafeHeadListener`-style derivation hook, the `optimism_safeHeadAtL1` RPC handler, and the CLI/config flag to enable it. The `SafeDbV1` trait is the seam those will build on.
